key_insight: Path Integral Stochastic Gradient Descent (PISGD) can reproduce the same tunneling-style escape scaling as quantum optimization, with escape governed by bounce action rather than barrier height.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a classical optimizer can sometimes overcome sharp, narrow energy barriers more efficiently than standard noise-driven methods, informing global optimization design.
method: Map optimization dynamics to path integrals and analyze escapes with instanton/bounce-action theory.
Adapt Kramers' escape-rate framework from ordinary space to path space for PISGD.
Compare scaling behavior on separable and nonseparable nonconvex potentials.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments showing the predicted bounce-action scaling for PISGD on both separable and nonseparable potentials.
watch_item: PISGD captures only incoherent tunneling, so it lacks the interference/coherence effects that may still advantage genuine quantum algorithms.
paper_title: From Quantum Tunneling to Classical Optimization through Instantons
